senses.definition: (weaponry) A firearm fired from the shoulder; improved range and accuracy is provided by a long, rifled barrel.

quotes.text: Still, a dozen men with rifles, and cartridges to match, stayed behind when they filed through a white aldea lying silent amid the cane, and the Sin Verguenza swung into slightly quicker stride.

senses.definition: (military, usually in the plural, dated) A rifleman.
(weaponry) An artillery piece with a rifled barrel.
A strip of wood covered with emery or a similar material, used for sharpening scythes.
(intransitive) To quickly search through many items (such as papers, the contents of a drawer, a pile of clothing).
examples: She made a mess when she rifled through the stack of papers, looking for the title document.

quotes.text: Thither repair at accustomed times their harlots […] not with empty hands, for they be as skilful in picking, rifling, and filching as the upright men.

senses.definition: (transitive) To search with intent to steal.

quotes.text: thine enemies […]shall ransack and rifle all the things of Edom; and shall search out all thy hidden commodities, and carry them away at once
quotes.reference: 1633, Joseph Hall, A paraphrase upon the hard texts of Scripture:

senses.definition: (transitive) To strip of goods; to rob; to pillage.

quotes.text: Stand, sir, and throw us that you have about ye: / If not, we'll make you sit and rifle you.

senses.definition: (transitive) To seize and bear away by force; to snatch away; to carry off.

quotes.text: Time shall rifle every youthful grace.

(transitive) To cause (a projectile, as a rifle bullet) to travel in a flat ballistic trajectory.
